facts.text: README describes the package as a ROS package that automatically configures a swarm robot simulator and says the documented start command is roslaunch swarm_stage_ros swarm_stage.launch.
README says that at the end of processing custom.world and controller.launch are generated, and that controller.launch starts the environment.
The generated controller.launch starts the external stage_ros/stageros node with custom.world, one posctrl node per robot, and one controller node with argument 3 in the shipped file.
The shipped swarm.yaml sets formation no, robots 3, position_controller yes, reference global and run yes; these are operator configuration values, not device bounds.
swarm_stage writes a controller.launch header that starts the ROS master and the stage_ros stageros node with launch/custom.world and respawn true.
The shipped controller.launch starts stageros with respawn true.
When the run parameter is yes, swarm_stage calls system(" killall stageros") and then system("roslaunch swarm_stage_ros controller.launch").
robot() writes one Stage model line per robot and, when position_controller is yes, writes a posctrl node with args="robot_<number>".
MainController::mainControl runs four loops of n/4 robots; each iteration advertises turtlesim::Pose on /robot_<i> with queue size 1000, sleeps 10 s and publishes that robot's target pose.
MainController::setPositions computes the target pose array from the requested robot count; it does not publish a feedback or stop topic.
PositionController::setTopics sets the subscription to /<nodeName> and the command publication to /<nodeName>/cmd_vel.
PositionController::mainControl advertises geometry_msgs::Twist on topicPub_ and subscribes to topicSub_ with queue size 15000.
PositionController::subCallback loops while the distance to the target is greater than 0.3 m, publishes Twist commands, and has no ROS cancellation, pause or stop check inside the loop.
PositionController::subCallback reads only msg->x and msg->y and computes the heading with atan2(msg->y - feedback_.y, msg->x - feedback_.x); it never reads the Pose theta field.
robotTransformed looks up the map to <node>/base_link transform and retries every second on a transform exception while ros::ok().
posctrl takes argv[1] as the node name, initialises the ROS node with it and passes it to setTopics.
The generated map include sets quit_time 3600 and paused 1 as static world properties.
CMakeLists builds the swarm_stage, controller and posctrl executables.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with no Stage step, posctrl loop, TF lookup or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it records advertise and publish messages on /robot_0 and runs no Stage world, stageros, posctrl follower, TF listener or ROS graph
only the /robot_0 target publication is bound; the generated launch also starts posctrl for robot_1 and robot_2 and the formation controller, which this package does not proxy
the target publication returns only {published: true, confirmed: false}; it is transmission evidence, not proof that posctrl received the target, computed a command, moved the robot or stopped it

no acknowledged stop, pause or reset service or action exists in the pinned clone; the simulator can only be killed by the process-level killall stageros call or by its static quit_time world property, neither of which is a ROS safe-state binding

Stage's own topics (/odom, /base_scan, /base_pose_ground_truth, /clock) come from the external stage_ros package and are not declared or cited by this clone, so this package exposes no odometry, laser or clock observation
the clone states no numeric arena or target-pose bound; x and y are operator_required and no site-limits.json is supplied here
the Pose theta field is sent as 0.0 and is not an operator input because the follower computes its heading from the target x/y direction and never reads the message theta

the built-in formation controller publishes only when the requested robot count is at least four (the four loops divide by four); the shipped robot count 3 therefore publishes no target, so an operator must publish the target or configure a count that the controller handles
live ROS, rosbridge, stage_ros, catkin_make and hardware are not run or validated here

safe_state.description: No acknowledged ROS stop is declared: the clone registers no stop, pause or reset service or action, so the e-stop fails with the latch held, which only refuses this driver's publications; Stage keeps running and each posctrl follower keeps publishing Twist commands until it is within 0.3 of its last target. A zero-Twist publication and killall stageros (respawned by the launch) are not safe-state evidence.
